title: Add probabilistic headroom sentinel and stagewise traffic bender
author: Aisha Malik
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent tail-latency regressions during low-headroom periods when multiple tenants simultaneously increase concurrency. Existing canary detectors flag regressions but do not provide an automated, smooth traffic-mitigation path that preserves throughput for healthy tenants. This change introduces two coupled pieces: (1) a probabilistic headroom sentinel that estimates per-tenant and cluster-wide headroom using Bayesian quantile forecasting and uncertainty bands, and (2) a stagewise traffic bender that performs graded, reversible traffic shaping (soft-throttle -> paced requeue -> selective shed) based on risk scoring and tenant SLAs.

Design summary: The headroom sentinel consumes real-time metrics (p50/p90/p99 latencies, in-flight requests, queue length, replica utilisation) and produces a probabilistic headroom score (0..1) with a 95% credible interval. The model uses an exponential-weighted quantile estimator combined with a small Bayesian linear update to account for sudden rate shifts. The score feeds the bender which applies a three-stage policy: Stage 0 (green) = normal routing; Stage 1 (amber) = adaptive pacing (delay tokens, reduce batch sizes) for noisy tenants; Stage 2 (red) = tenant-scoped soft-throttle with polite retry headers and degraded-quality fallback routing. Policies are configurable by SLO weight, customer tier, and region.

Why this is different: Instead of hard circuit breakers or naive rate caps, the staging is probabilistic and budget-aware: it respects per-tenant headroom budgets and can be undone automatically when posterior probability of sufficient headroom recovers. The system is designed to be robust to brief measurement noise and to avoid cascading throttle loops by coordinating via a cluster-backed lease and cooldown window.

Checklist: 
- [x] Core sentinel algorithm implemented (go/service/headroom)
- [x] Stagewise bender runtime and policy engine (go/runtime/traffic_bender)
- [x] Integration tests for single-tenant and multi-tenant scenarios (tests/perf/headroom_test.go)
- [x] E2E canary wiring and dashboards (infra/observability/dashboards/headroom.jsonnet)
- [x] Docs + rollout guide (docs/canaries/headroom-sentinel.md)
- [x] Telemetry (metrics/tracing) and alerting rules (monitoring/alerts/headroom.yaml)
- [x] Safety: opt-in via feature flag and default disabled for dedicated/private clusters

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind perf.canary.headroom.enabled (default=false). Rollout steps: 1) internal canary in perf-canary test cluster (1 week), 2) opt-in beta for 5 enterprise tenants, 3) full opt-in for new clusters with default off for existing tenants. We will monitor p99 latency regressions, throughput delta, and throttle events.

Compatibility and risk: The sentinel is read-only to routing decisions until the bender is explicitly enabled. When enabled, the bender emits non-disruptive headers and metrics for 24h as a dry-run before enforcing Stage 1. We documented escalation playbooks and added an emergency kill-switch that disables bender at the cluster control-plane level.

References: ENG-1919 for product requirements, SUP-8421 for customer incident that motivated the change.

review_comments: Mateo Chen (reviewer): The probabilistic model looks solid but we should avoid costly locks in the hot path. Can we use optimistic reads with compare-and-swap for the lease?
Author (Aisha): Switched to optimistic lease CAS and added benchmarks showing <1% CPU overhead at 10k rps. See commit g4b6d88.
Priya Rao (reviewer): We need clearer telemetry for false positives (cases where sentinel fires but no real regret). Add a synthetic probe metric.
Author (Aisha): Added headroom.synthetic_probe.{success,fail} metrics and an alert that triggers if false positive rate > 10% over 1h.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Tests look good but add a multi-tenant integration scenario with asymmetric load growth.
Author (Aisha): Added test case and tuned cool-down window from 60s to 90s for safer de-escalation.
Mateo Chen (approval): Approving after the CAS change and added telemetry.

release_notes:
- Added a probabilistic headroom sentinel to detect low-headroom windows and a stagewise traffic bender to gracefully mitigate tenant-driven overloads.
- Feature is behind perf.canary.headroom.enabled and defaulted off.
- Admins can opt-in per-cluster and there is an emergency kill-switch in the control plane.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag in a staging cluster first. Dashboards: observability->headroom sentinel. Watch p99 latency and headroom.synthetic_probe metrics. If rollout causes unexpected throughput drop, toggle perf.canary.headroom.enabled to false at control plane.
